# Reproducible presentation of the Boulesteix et al. study

This document serves as the presentation of a reproducible research compendium for the simulation study by @boulesteixIntroductionStatisticalSimulations2020. It will contain the r source code that was used as well as its results.

All data can be found in the `./data` folder.

## R Code

### 1. Load the required libraries:
```{r libraries}
#| output: false

library(Hmisc)
library(mice)
library(tidyverse)
```

### 2. Load, merge and prepare the data (downloaded from [CDC - NHANES](https://wwwn.cdc.gov/nchs/nhanes/continuousnhanes/default.aspx?BeginYear=2015)):
```{r data}
#| output: false
#| cache: true

d1 <- sasxport.get("./data/DEMO_I.XPT")
d2 <- sasxport.get("./data/BPX_I.XPT")
d3 <- sasxport.get("./data/BMX_I.XPT")
d4 <- sasxport.get("./data/GHB_I.XPT")
d5 <- sasxport.get("./data/TCHOL_I.XPT")
d1.t <- subset(d1,select=c("seqn","riagendr","ridageyr"))
d2.t <- subset(d2,select=c("seqn","bpxsy1"))
d3.t <- subset(d3,select=c("seqn","bmxbmi"))
d4.t <- subset(d4,select=c("seqn","lbxgh"))
d5.t <- subset(d5,select=c("seqn","lbdtcsi"))
d <- merge(d1.t,d2.t)
d <- merge(d,d3.t)
d <- merge(d,d4.t)
d <- merge(d,d5.t)

# rename variables:
# RIAGENDR - Gender
# RIDAGEYR - Age in years at screening
# BPXSY1 - Systolic: Blood pres (1st rdg) mm Hg
# BMXBMI - Body Mass Index (kg/m**2)
# LBDTCSI - Total Cholesterol (mmol/L)
# LBXGH - Glycohemoglobin (%)
d$age <- d$ridageyr
d$sex <- d$riagendr
d$bp <- d$bpxsy1
d$bmi <- d$bmxbmi
d$HbA1C <- d$lbxgh
d$chol <- d$lbdtcsi
d$age[d$age<18] <- NA

# select complete cases:
dc <- cc(subset(d,select=c("age","sex","bmi","HbA1C","bp")))
```

### 3. Analyze the data:
```{r analysis}
#| output: false

s1 <- summary(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
ci1 <- confint(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
s2 <- summary(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + bmi + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
ci2 <- confint(lm(bp ~ HbA1C + bmi + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc))
```

### 4. Simulation of measurement error:

```{r simulation}
#| cache: true
#| output: false

set.seed(12345)

ref <- lm(bp ~ HbA1C + bmi + age + as.factor(sex), data=dc)$coef[2]
n.sim <- 1e3
perc.me.exp <- seq(0,.5,.1)
perc.me.conf<- seq(0,.5,.1)
scenarios <- expand.grid(perc.me.exp,perc.me.conf)
var.exp <- var(dc$HbA1C)
var.conf <- var(dc$bmi)
n <- dim(dc)[1]
beta.hat <- matrix(ncol=dim(scenarios)[1], nrow=n.sim)
for (k in 1:n.sim){
  set.seed(k)
  for (i in 1:dim(scenarios)[1]){
    var.me.exp <- var.exp*scenarios[i,1]/(1-scenarios[i,1])
    var.me.conf <- var.conf*scenarios[i,2]/(1-scenarios[i,2])
    dc$HbA1C.me <- dc$HbA1C + rnorm(dim(dc)[1], 0, sqrt(var.me.exp) )
    dc$bmi.me <- dc$bmi + rnorm(dim(dc)[1], 0, sqrt(var.me.conf) )
    beta.hat[k,i] <- lm(bp ~ HbA1C.me + age + bmi.me + as.factor(sex), data=dc)$coef[2]
  }}
```

### 5. Create figure:
```{r figure_prep}
#| output: false

tot.mat <- cbind(100*scenarios,apply(beta.hat,2,mean))
colnames(tot.mat) <- c("me.exp","me.conf","estimate")
```

```{r figure_plot}
matrix_plot <- ggplot(tot.mat, aes(me.exp, me.conf)) +
  geom_tile(color="white",aes(fill = estimate)) +
  geom_text(aes(label = round(estimate, 2))) +
  scale_fill_gradient2(low="#D55E00",mid="white",high = "#56B4E9", midpoint=ref) +
  labs(x=paste("% of total variance of HbA1c due to measurement error"),
       y=paste("% of total variance of BMI due to measurement error")) +
  coord_equal()+
  scale_y_continuous(breaks=unique(tot.mat[,1]))+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks=unique(tot.mat[,1]))+
  theme(panel.background = element_rect(fill='white', colour='grey'),
        plot.title=element_text(hjust=0),
        axis.ticks=element_blank(),
        axis.title=element_text(size=12),
        axis.text=element_text(size=10),
        legend.title=element_text(size=12),
        legend.text=element_text(size=10))
```

## Results

From the data, the average effect of a patient's glycohemoglobin level (HbA1C, in %) on their systolic blood pressure (1st rdg), controlling for their age and sex was estimated to be `{r} round(s1$coefficients[2,1], 2)` (95% CI [`{r} round(ci1[2,1], 2)`; `{r} round(ci1[2,2], 2)`], p < .001).

The simulation of the measurement error is visualized in the following matrix plot:
```{r}
#| echo: false

matrix_plot
```
